# Async Swap

An on-chain order book and matching engine built as a Uniswap v4 hook: limit orders against USDC, matched by price, priority bid and time.

- [AsyncSwap](/reference/src/AsyncSwap): Uniswap v4 hook that converts an exact-input swap into an open async order: the maker deposits their input via `_beforeSwap`. Crossing orders settle directly at the resting limit; fillers settle unmatched orders.
- [FeeVault](/reference/src/FeeVault): Holds and redeems protocol fee claims, never maker escrow.
- [ImmutableState](/reference/src/ImmutableState): A collection of immutable state variables, commonly used across multiple contracts
- [MatchingEngine](/reference/src/MatchingEngine): Standalone price-time matching harness. It maintains a radix-indexed limit book and emits deterministic fill instructions.
- [NativeClaims](/reference/src/NativeClaims): Redeems the caller's PoolManager native ETH claims to a chosen recipient.
- [Router](/reference/src/Router): Thin entrypoint for makers (`swap`), fillers (`fillOrder`), and makers cancelling orders (`cancelOrder`). All three actions go through `IPoolManager.unlock` so the hook can operate on PM debts. Native payouts/refunds are PoolManager claims (ID 0), redeemable through NativeClaims after approval; ERC20 payouts remain direct.
- [TokenClaims](/reference/src/TokenClaims): Redeems the caller's PoolManager currency claims to a chosen recipient.
- [BaseHook](/reference/src/BaseHook): abstract contract for hook implementations
- [IFeeOwner](/reference/src/IFeeOwner)
- [ISignatureTransfer](/reference/src/interfaces/ISignatureTransfer): Minimal subset of Uniswap Permit2's SignatureTransfer interface used by the Router. Canonical Permit2 lives at 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 on every chain.
- [AsyncFiller](/reference/src/libraries/AsyncFiller): Stores open async orders and settles fills against them.
- [AsyncMatching](/reference/src/libraries/AsyncMatching): Linked matching module operating on the hook's order and radix-book storage.
- [CurrencySettler](/reference/src/libraries/CurrencySettler): Production copy of v4-core's test-only `CurrencySettler`, using safe transfers so tokens that return no data from `transfer` / `transferFrom` (e.g. USDT) settle correctly.
- [EligiblePrice](/reference/src/libraries/EligiblePrice): Exact-price summaries on a priority-key radix tree.
- [OrderSignatures](/reference/src/libraries/OrderSignatures): EIP-712 types for signed AsyncSwap actions. Every type spells out the maker, both tokens and the amounts so wallets render a readable message instead of opaque calldata.
- [RadixPriceTree](/reference/src/libraries/RadixPriceTree): Patricia radix index for uint128 price levels. Inserts and removals traverse at most 128 branch bits; each distinct price creates one leaf and at most one branch node. Node ids released by `remove` are recycled by later inserts, so the id counter only grows with the peak number of simultaneously stored prices and can never be exhausted in practice (2^31 simultaneous levels).
- [AsyncOrderLibrary](/reference/src/types/AsyncOrderLibrary): Helpers attached to AsyncOrder for identity and pricing.
- [AsyncOrder](/reference/src/types/AsyncOrder): Represents an async order for a swap in the Uniswap V4 pool.

![Async Swap](/assets/async-swap-banner.png)

# Async Swap

Async Swap is an on-chain order book and matching engine built as a Uniswap v4 hook. Traders set a
limit price for assets paired with USDC. Orders match with other traders or with the pool's active
liquidity, and anyone can permissionlessly fill a resting order.

* **Price, then bid, then time.** Book matching ranks orders by price. Among orders at the same
  price, a higher escrowed USDC priority bid goes first, and earlier orders break equal bids.
* **Orders rest until they execute.** Unfilled amounts stay open for later matching, a pool fill,
  a filler, repricing or cancellation.
* **No swap touches the curve directly.** Every swap becomes an order. The only AMM swaps are the
  ones the hook makes to fill a resting order from pool liquidity, and those pay active LPs a
  0.30% fee.
* **Proceeds you can always claim.** A book match credits both sides as PoolManager claims, which
  you redeem to any address through `TokenClaims` (ERC-20) or `NativeClaims` (ETH). A recipient a
  token refuses cannot block matching.

# Async Swap protocol map

Async Swap is a Uniswap v4 hook that turns exact-input swaps into resting limit orders. This page
describes the whole protocol in diagrams: which contracts exist, where funds sit, how an order is
created, matched, filled, repriced and cancelled, and who is allowed to do what. Every box names a
contract, library or function in `src/`, so the diagrams can be checked against the code.

## 1. Components

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Actors
        Maker["Maker<br/>(places, reprices, cancels)"]
        Filler["Filler<br/>(fills a resting order)"]
        Relayer["Relayer<br/>(submits signed orders)"]
        Keeper["Anyone<br/>(matchBook, fillFromPoolLiquidity)"]
        LP["v4 LP<br/>(adds range liquidity)"]
        Owner["Protocol owner<br/>(FeeVault.collect, sweep, minimum order size)"]
    end

    subgraph Periphery
        Router["Router.sol<br/>swap · swapWithSig · fillOrder<br/>cancelOrder · cancelWithSig<br/>matchBook · fillFromPoolLiquidity"]
        Permit2["Permit2<br/>permitWitnessTransferFrom"]
        NativeClaims["NativeClaims.sol<br/>redeem native claims (ID 0)"]
        TokenClaims["TokenClaims.sol<br/>redeem ERC-20 claims"]
    end

    subgraph Core
        PM["Uniswap v4 PoolManager<br/>unlock · swap<br/>ERC-6909 claims"]
        Hook["AsyncSwap.sol (hook)<br/>beforeInitialize · beforeSwap<br/>beforeAddLiquidity<br/>matchNewOrder · executeOrder<br/>updatePrice · cancelOrder<br/>setExecutor(WithSig)"]
        Matching["AsyncMatching.sol<br/>external library, delegatecall<br/>addOrder · match · fill · cancel<br/>updatePrice · fillFromPool"]
        Filler_["AsyncFiller.sol<br/>State: orders, isExecutor<br/>Book: bids, asks, levels"]
        Radix["RadixPriceTree.sol<br/>best bid / best ask<br/>priority tree per level"]
        Sigs["OrderSignatures.sol<br/>EIP-712 types · Permit2 witness"]
        Vault["FeeVault.sol<br/>owns protocol fee claims in PoolManager<br/>collect(currency, recipient)"]
    end

    Maker -->|swap, cancelOrder| Router
    Maker -->|setExecutor, updatePrice| Hook
    Relayer -->|swapWithSig, cancelWithSig| Router
    Filler -->|fillOrder maxPrice| Router
    Keeper -->|matchBook, fillFromPoolLiquidity| Router
    LP -->|modifyLiquidity| PM
    Owner -->|collect| Vault
    Owner -->|sweep, setMinOrder| Hook

    Router -->|unlock → unlockCallback| PM
    Router -->|signed input| Permit2
    Permit2 -->|transfer input| PM
    PM -->|beforeSwap hookData| Hook
    Router -->|matchNewOrder, executeOrder,<br/>cancelOrder, matchBook,<br/>tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity| Hook
    Hook -.->|delegatecall| Matching
    Matching --> Filler_
    Filler_ --> Radix
    Hook --> Sigs
    Router --> Sigs
    Hook -->|mint / take / burn / settle| PM
    PM -.->|accounting credit, not a contract call| Vault
    Vault -->|burn + take| PM
    Maker -->|redeem| NativeClaims
    NativeClaims -->|burn ID 0, send ETH| PM
    Maker -->|redeem| TokenClaims
    TokenClaims -->|burn claim, send ERC-20| PM
```

Every pool that uses the hook must contain the chain's USDC (`numeraire`) and use the dynamic-fee flag
(`beforeInitialize`). `beforeAddLiquidity` is a pass-through: anyone may add ordinary v4 range
positions, and they are the inventory for the LP-fill path. No swap ever reaches the AMM curve
directly, because `beforeSwap` consumes the whole input as an order; the only AMM swaps are the ones
the hook itself performs when it fills a resting order from pool liquidity. The standalone
`MatchingEngine.sol` is a benchmark harness and is not deployed.

FeeVault owns claims recorded in PoolManager. Crediting those claims does not call FeeVault.

## 2. Where funds live

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph PoolManager["PoolManager (custody)"]
        Escrow["ERC-6909 claims owned by the hook<br/>one balance per currency<br/>= Σ open orders' remaining input<br/>+ escrowed priority bids"]
        Fees["ERC-6909 claims owned by FeeVault<br/>= accrued 30 bps fill fees<br/>+ settled priority bids"]
        User["ERC-6909 claims owned by makers / fillers<br/>match proceeds and dust refunds (any currency),<br/>native fill proceeds (claim ID 0)"]
        Reserves["Pool reserves<br/>v4 LP positions"]
    end
    MakerW["Maker wallet"] -->|input on swap| Escrow
    Escrow -->|cancel: full remainder| MakerW
    Escrow -->|match: input as claims| User
    Escrow -->|fill: input| CounterW["Filler wallet"]
    CounterW -->|fill: output| MakerW
    FillerW["Filler wallet"] -->|protocol fee from gross output payment| Fees
    Escrow -->|priority bids| Fees
    Fees -->|collect| OwnerW["Owner-chosen recipient"]
    User -->|TokenClaims.redeem /<br/>NativeClaims.redeem| MakerW
```

Fees, by path: an order-to-order match charges nothing; a filler fill (`Router.fillOrder`) pays
the maker's live minimum plus 30 bps of gross output, and that fee lands in the FeeVault as claims;
an LP fill charges the 30 bps dynamic LP fee to the active v4 positions. `calculateHookFee` is zero.
Priority bids are escrowed as hook claims by `addOrder` and settle to the FeeVault: the filled share
as input fills, the rest when the order closes. They never go to LPs, so liquidity added just before
a settlement earns none of them.

An order-to-order match pays both sides, and returns any remainder left below the pool minimum, as
PoolManager claims rather than token transfers, so a recipient a token refuses cannot block matching.
Holders redeem ERC-20 claims through `TokenClaims` and native claims through `NativeClaims`, to any
recipient, after approving the redeemer for that claim id. Filler fills and LP fills pay the maker's
ERC-20 output directly. Minting bid
claims creates hook debt immediately; the PoolManager unlock must settle that debt, including for
custom executors. The Router pays it with `settleFor(hook)`. All pools rank equal prices by remaining
bid, then sequence. There is no FIFO mode or mode switch.

The accounting invariant is fuzzed by the matching invariant suites: the hook's claim balance for
each currency equals the sum of remaining inputs of open orders plus escrowed bids, and nothing is
created or destroyed by a match. The hook's own token balance is zero between transactions, so
`sweep` can only move stranded ETH or tokens sent to the hook by mistake, never escrow.

## 3. Placing an order

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    participant M as Maker
    participant R as Router
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant H as AsyncSwap hook
    participant AM as AsyncMatching (delegatecall)

    M->>H: setExecutor(poolId, Router, true) — once per pool
    M->>R: swap(order, UserParams)
    Note over R: checks owner == msg.sender, executor == Router,<br/>amountOutMin and priorityFee match the order
    R->>PM: unlock(Swap)
    PM->>R: unlockCallback
    R->>PM: swap(key, exactInput = -amountIn, hookData)
    PM->>H: beforeSwap(sender = Router, params, hookData)
    H->>PM: take(input, hook, amountIn, claims = true)
    H->>AM: addOrder(id, owner, amountIn, amountOutMin, isBuy, priorityFee)
    AM->>PM: mint numeraire bid claims to hook, hook owes bid
    Note over AM: salt assigned by the hook, priceKey = WAD ratio,<br/>order linked into the bid or ask level
    H-->>PM: BeforeSwapDelta consumes the whole input
    R->>PM: settle input from maker (ERC-20 transferFrom or forwarded ETH)
    opt priorityFee > 0
        R->>PM: settleFor(hook) with USDC bid
    end
    R->>H: matchNewOrder(order)
    H->>AM: match up to 8 crossing resting orders
    opt Incoming order still open
        H->>H: guarded self-call for LP fill
        H->>AM: try full remainder against active LP liquidity
        AM-->>H: Fill succeeds or LP attempt rolls back
    end
    H-->>R: Matched pair count
    R-->>PM: Callback complete
    PM-->>R: Unlock complete with settled deltas
    R-->>M: Transaction succeeds
    Note over H: emits AsyncOrderCreated, AsyncOrdersMatched / AsyncOrderLiquidityFilled
```

Signed orders follow the same path through `swapWithSig`. The maker signs one Permit2
`PermitWitnessTransferFrom` whose witness is `OrderSignatures.hashOrder(order)`, so the signature
both moves the input and commits to the order. A relayer can also attach a signed `SetExecutor` grant
for the maker's first order on a pool.

## 4. Everything after placement

Filler fills, book continuation, LP retries, repricing, cancellation, pool setup, native-claim
redemption and fee collection are drawn step by step in
[`contract-call-sequences.md`](/protocol/contract-call-sequences); the lifecycle and priority-bid flowcharts
are in [`order-lifecycle.md`](/protocol/order-lifecycle). Three facts to keep in mind while reading them:

* An order-to-order match charges no fee. The 30 bps protocol fee is paid by the filler on top of the
  maker's live minimum and is credited to the FeeVault as ERC-6909 claims inside the PoolManager; the
  LP-fill path instead charges the 30 bps dynamic LP fee to active v4 positions. `calculateHookFee`
  is zero.
* `updatePrice` only re-ranks the order in the book. It needs no PoolManager unlock and triggers no
  matching; a later crossing order, `matchBook`, a filler or an LP retry has to execute it.
* `matchNewOrder` is gated by a transient slot that `beforeSwap` writes for
  the current transaction. `executeOrder`, `cancelOrder` and `tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity` check
  `isExecutor[maker][caller]` instead.

An order's identity is `keccak(chainId, poolId, owner, zeroForOne, salt)`. The hook assigns the
salt at creation and emits it in `AsyncOrderCreated`; later calls recompute the id from the maker's
struct, so a maker needs the event or an indexer to cancel or reprice.

## 5. Authorization

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph MakerRights["Maker (order.owner)"]
        m1["swap / cancelOrder via Router<br/>(msg.sender must be owner)"]
        m2["updatePrice (msg.sender must be owner)"]
        m3["setExecutor / revoke"]
        m4["sign: Permit2 order witness,<br/>SetExecutor, UpdatePrice, CancelOrder (EIP-712)"]
    end
    subgraph ExecutorRights["Registered executor (the Router)"]
        e1["beforeSwap sender must equal hookData.executor<br/>and be authorised by the maker"]
        e2["executeOrder, cancelOrder, tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity<br/>require isExecutor[maker][caller], inside the unlock"]
        e3["matchNewOrder: only the executor<br/>recorded by beforeSwap in the same tx (transient slot)"]
    end
    subgraph OwnerRights["Protocol owner (two-step transfer)"]
        o1["FeeVault.collect(currency, recipient)"]
        o2["sweep(currency, to) — hook's raw balance only"]
        o3["setMinOrder(key, minimum), setDefaultMinOrder(minimum)"]
        o4["no pause, no upgrade, no access to escrow"]
    end
    subgraph Public["Anyone"]
        p1["matchBook(key, 1..8)"]
        p2["fillFromPoolLiquidity(order)"]
        p3["fillOrder(order, maxPrice) — pays the maker"]
        p4["submit a maker's signed order or cancel"]
    end
```

Signed maker actions use unordered nonces: `AsyncSwap.nonceUsed` for `SetExecutor` and
`UpdatePrice`, `Router.cancelNonceUsed` for `CancelOrder`, and Permit2's own nonces for order
witnesses. The Permit2 witness binds maker, both tokens, amounts, bid and pool; it leaves out
`sqrtPrice` (never read, the hook consumes the whole swap) and `salt` (assigned by the hook).

## 6. Deployment shape

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    D["CREATE2 deployer<br/>0x4e59…956C"] -->|fixed salt| Lib["AsyncMatching library<br/>same address on every chain"]
    D -->|mined salt: flags + 0x91 prefix| Hook["AsyncSwap hook<br/>constructor(PoolManager, USDC, owner)"]
    Hook -->|constructor| Vault["FeeVault"]
    Owner["Deployer / owner"] -->|CREATE| Router["Router(PoolManager, hook, Permit2)"]
    Lib -.->|linked into bytecode| Hook
    Owner -->|CREATE, separate script| NC["NativeClaims(PoolManager)"]
    Owner -->|CREATE, separate script| TC["TokenClaims(PoolManager)"]
    Hook -->|initialize| Pool["Pool: USDC × asset<br/>dynamic fee flag, hook address"]
```

`script/deploy.sh <chain-key> [dry-run|broadcast|verify]` runs this sequence against
`script/config/chains.json`. On chains whose gas token has an ERC-20 twin (Arc: native USDC and
`0x3600…0000` are one balance) never initialize a native-currency pool; pair the ERC-20 USDC with a
normal ERC-20 asset.

See also [`price-key-crossing.md`](/protocol/price-key-crossing) for how truncated price keys decide
whether two orders cross, and [mainnet readiness](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/MAINNET_READINESS.md) for the release gate.

# Order lifecycle and priority bids

Current behavior, checked against the contract source. See also [contract call sequences](/protocol/contract-call-sequences) and the [README](/).

## Order lifecycle

These diagrams describe the current source, not a deployment or mainnet-readiness guarantee. Book matching ranks the best opposing price first; higher escrowed USDC bids break ties at that price, followed by earlier submission. Private fills and explicit LP retries target a specific order and do not enforce the book's global priority queue.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Submit order: input amount, minimum output, USDC bid"] --> D["Require pool minimum and tiered bid"]
    D --> E["Validate executor; escrow input and bid at creation"]
    E --> F["Match best opposing prices first; up to 8 pairs"]
    F --> G["Same-price ties: highest remaining bid, then earliest sequence"]
    G --> H["Settle executable crossing pairs; reduce orders and settle bid shares"]
    H --> I{"Incoming order still open?"}
    I -- "No" --> Z["Order closed; return unused input if any"]
    I -- "Yes" --> J["Try remaining input against pool liquidity"]
    J --> K{"Full remaining input consumed and minimum output met?"}
    K -- "Yes" --> L["Settle pool fill; 30 bps LP fee; settle remaining bid"]
    L --> Z
    K -- "No / attempt reverts" --> M["Roll back LP attempt only; keep remaining order open"]
    M -- "New crossing order or Router.matchBook" --> N["Bounded book matching; partial fills can remain open"]
    N -- "Remainder" --> M
    N -- "Input exhausted or remainder below pool minimum" --> Z
    M -- "Router.fillFromPoolLiquidity" --> J
    M -- "Private filler chooses order" --> O["Check live minimum plus protocol fee against filler maxPrice"]
    O --> P["Filler funds output; settle full remainder and bid; close order"]
    P --> Z
    M -- "Maker reprices" --> Q["Update minimum; re-enter book with fresh time priority"]
    Q --> M
    M -- "Authorized cancellation" --> R["Return remaining input; settle remaining bid; close order"]
    R --> Z
```

If no executable crossing pair exists, the initial matching pass leaves the order unchanged before the LP attempt. `Router.matchBook` accepts a bound of 1–8 pairs and does not itself retry LP liquidity. An LP retry does not require the order to be first in the book. Private fills require a maker-authorized executor (normally the Router); the filler supplies the live minimum plus the protocol fee in the same transaction. That protocol fee is separate from the LP fee on pool-liquidity fills. Book-match proceeds, and input returned below the pool minimum, are credited as PoolManager claims in every currency, redeemable through `TokenClaims` (ERC-20) or `NativeClaims` (ETH); native fill proceeds and refunds are claims too. Filler and LP fills pay ERC-20 output directly.

Sources: [Router](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/Router.sol), [AsyncSwap](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/AsyncSwap.sol), [AsyncMatching](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol), and [AsyncFiller](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol).

## Priority-bid settlement

Priority bids are escrowed in USDC and are **non-refundable**. The creation minimum is `min(0.10 USDC, 0.1% of the order’s USDC notional)`, rounded down to base units. An unlock cannot finish with an unpaid bid debt. They rank same-price orders within the book; they do not purchase block inclusion or transaction ordering from the chain.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Escrow USDC bid as PoolManager claims"] --> B{"Order event"}
    B -- "Book match" --> C["Settle proportional bid share for each order's consumed input"]
    C --> D{"Remaining order meets pool minimum?"}
    D -- "Yes" --> E["Keep unspent bid escrowed; update remaining order and rank"]
    E --> B
    D -- "No" --> F["Settle all remaining bid; return unused input; close order"]
    B -- "Successful LP or private fill" --> F
    B -- "Authorized cancellation" --> F
    B -- "Reprice" --> E
    C --> G{"Bid amount to settle is nonzero?"}
    F --> G
    G -- "No" --> H["No bid transfer"]
    G -- "Yes" --> K["Transfer bid claims to protocol FeeVault"]
    K --> L["Commit with the order operation in the same unlock"]
    H --> L
    L -. "Any later revert" .-> M["Roll back operation and bid settlement together"]
```

For each book match, the settled share is `floor(remainingBid * inputUsed / remainingInputBeforeFill)`. If the order terminates, any residual bid is settled too; it is never returned to the maker. A partial fill can leave a bid below the creation minimum. Its remaining bid determines its new same-price rank. If the remaining price key changes, it also receives a fresh sequence number. Maker repricing always assigns fresh time priority without refunding the bid.

Bids always go to the FeeVault, whatever liquidity is in range, so liquidity added for the moment of settlement captures none of them. A failed LP self-call rolls back that attempt, including its fee and bid changes, while preserving prior successful book matches in the surrounding transaction. A revert of the surrounding transaction rolls everything back.

Sources: [`_reduceAfterMatch` and `_settleMatchedPriorityFee`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol), [`settlePriorityFee`, `fill`, and `cancel`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol). The [original chat diagrams](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/docs/historical-matching-diagrams.md) are retained as historical references.

# Contract call sequences

The [protocol overview](/protocol/overview#3-placing-an-order) contains the short order sequence; this page contains the detailed sequences. See [order lifecycle and priority bids](/protocol/order-lifecycle) for the flowcharts.

Solid arrows are calls or actions; dashed arrows are returns or delivered results. Each sequence groups related transactions; it is not one transaction from top to bottom. The app and wallet represent the user interface, not trusted settlement components. An indexer may observe emitted events for discovery, but neither an API nor an indexer is required by the contracts.

`AsyncMatching` is a linked external library called in the hook's context. `AsyncFiller`, the price tree, and currency-settlement helpers operate on that same context; they are not independent custodians. Arrows from the matching library to PoolManager therefore execute as the hook. ERC-6909 claims and LP fee accounting live inside PoolManager.

### User order, book matching, and LP fallback

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Maker
    participant App as App
    participant Wallet as Maker wallet
    actor Relayer
    participant Router
    participant Hook as AsyncSwap hook
    participant Match as AsyncMatching / AsyncFiller
    participant Permit as Permit2
    participant Token as ERC-20 / USDC
    participant PM as PoolManager
    actor Counterparty as Resting maker
    participant Vault as FeeVault

    User->>App: Choose asset, input amount, minimum output, and bid
    App->>Wallet: Request approval, authorization, and order confirmation
    opt Router not yet authorized for this maker and pool
        Wallet->>Hook: setExecutor(poolId, Router, true)
        Hook-->>Wallet: Authorization recorded
    end
    Note over Wallet,Token: Direct ERC-20 input needs Router approval, signed input needs Permit2 approval.<br/>A nonzero USDC bid separately needs Router approval.
    alt Direct order, including native ETH input
        Wallet->>Router: swap(order, userData), exact ETH value if native
    else Signed ERC-20 order
        Wallet-->>Relayer: Permit2 order-witness signature and optional executor grant
        Relayer->>Router: swapWithSig(order, permit, grant)
        opt Signed executor grant needed
            Router->>Hook: setExecutorWithSig(...)
            Hook-->>Router: Grant validated and recorded
        end
    end
    Router->>PM: unlock(create action)
    PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
    Router->>PM: swap(exact input, hook data)
    PM->>Hook: beforeSwap(...)
    Hook->>PM: mint input escrow claims to hook
    Hook->>Match: Validate and add order to price book
    Match->>PM: mint bid escrow claims to hook, hook owes bid
    Match-->>Hook: Order recorded
    Note over Hook,Match: AsyncOrderCreated event, order is not matched until input and bid funding finish.
    Hook-->>PM: beforeSwap selector and custom accounting delta
    PM-->>Router: Swap delta
    alt Direct input funding
        Router->>PM: Settle input using ERC-20 transfer or forwarded ETH
    else Permit2 input funding
        Router->>PM: sync(input token)
        Router->>Permit: permitWitnessTransferFrom(order witness)
        Permit->>Token: transferFrom(maker, PoolManager, input)
        Token-->>Permit: Transfer succeeds
        Permit-->>Router: Signature and transfer accepted
        Router->>PM: settle()
    end
    opt Nonzero priority bid
        Router->>PM: sync(USDC)
        Router->>Token: transferFrom(maker, PoolManager, bid)
        Token-->>Router: Transfer succeeds
        Router->>PM: settleFor(hook)
    end
    Router->>Hook: matchNewOrder(order)
    Hook->>Match: matchIncoming(...)
    loop Up to 8 executable crossing pairs
        Match->>Match: Best bid and best ask across the whole book (price, then bid, then time)
        Match->>Match: Reduce both orders before any payout
        Match->>PM: Settle filled bid shares to FeeVault
        Match->>PM: Burn input claims and credit both order legs as claims
        PM-->>Wallet: Proceeds as claims (any currency)
        PM-->>Counterparty: Proceeds as claims (any currency)
        Note over Match,Vault: Re-rank remainders. A remainder below the pool minimum is returned as claims<br/>and its residual bid goes to FeeVault.
    end
    Match-->>Hook: Matched pair count
    opt Incoming order still has a remainder
        Hook->>Hook: External self-call fillOrderFromPoolLiquidity(order, id)
        Hook->>Match: fillFromPoolLiquidity(...)
        Match->>PM: Burn remaining input claims, temporarily set 30 bps LP fee
        Match->>PM: swap(remaining exact input)
        Note over Hook,PM: Hook-originated swap skips this hook's callbacks, it does not create another order.
        PM-->>Match: Actual input and output deltas
        Match->>PM: Restore previous LP fee
        alt Full remaining input consumed and minimum output met
            Match->>PM: Pay output, settle remaining bid to FeeVault
            PM-->>Wallet: ERC-20 proceeds or native claims
            Match-->>Hook: Order removed, liquidity fill event
        else Insufficient liquidity, partial execution, or limit not met
            Match-->>Hook: Self-call reverts, caught by matchNewOrder
            Note over Hook,PM: Only LP attempt rolls back, prior book fills and open remainder survive.
        end
    end
    Hook-->>Router: Matched pair count
    Router-->>PM: Callback complete
    PM-->>Router: Unlock completes if all currency deltas are settled
    Router-->>Wallet: Direct transaction succeeds
    Note over Wallet,Relayer: For signed submission, the transaction result returns to the submitter instead.
```

The LP fee accrues through PoolManager's position accounting. Priority bids are not paid to LPs: every settled bid goes to the FeeVault. LPs do not receive an external callback on every fill.

### Private fillers, continuation, repricing, and cancellation

These are alternative actions on open orders. Private fills and LP retries require the Router to remain authorized by the maker. Book continuation is permissionless and processes at most eight pairs per call.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Maker as Maker / wallet
    actor Caller as Filler or public caller
    participant Router
    participant Hook as AsyncSwap hook
    participant Match as AsyncMatching / AsyncFiller
    participant Token as Output ERC-20
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant Vault as FeeVault

    alt Private filler settles a specific order
        Caller->>Hook: asyncOrderInfo(poolId, orderId)
        Hook-->>Caller: Live remaining input and minimum output
        Caller->>Router: fillOrder(order, maxPrice, data)
        Note over Caller,Hook: Native output requires exact gross ETH, forwarded by Router to hook before unlock.<br/>ERC-20 output requires filler approval to Router.
        Router->>PM: unlock(fill action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>Hook: Read live minimum and calculate protocol fee
        Hook-->>Router: Net minimum and fee
        Router->>Router: Require gross output no greater than maxPrice
        opt ERC-20 output
            Router->>PM: sync(output token)
            Router->>Token: transferFrom(filler, PoolManager, gross output)
            Token-->>Router: Transfer succeeds
            Router->>PM: settleFor(hook)
        end
        Router->>Hook: executeOrder(order, filler)
        Hook->>Match: fill(...), validate executor and open order
        Match->>PM: Settle output, pay maker net minimum
        PM-->>Maker: ERC-20 output or native claims
        Match->>PM: mint protocol-fee claims to FeeVault
        Note over PM,Vault: Claims are credited inside PoolManager, FeeVault is not called during a fill.
        Match->>PM: Burn input escrow, pay filler remaining input
        PM-->>Caller: ERC-20 input or native claims
        Match->>PM: Settle remaining bid to FeeVault
        Match-->>Hook: Order closed, AsyncOrderFilled event
        Hook-->>Router: Fill complete
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Caller: Transaction succeeds
    else Continue a crossed book
        Caller->>Router: matchBook(key, maxMatches from 1 to 8)
        Router->>PM: unlock(match action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>Hook: matchBook(key, maxMatches)
        Hook->>Match: Match best bid and ask, settle pairs and bids
        Match->>PM: Burn claims, pay counterparties, settle bid shares
        Match-->>Hook: Matched pair count
        Hook-->>Router: Matched pair count
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Caller: Transaction succeeds
    else Retry a specific order against LP liquidity
        Caller->>Router: fillFromPoolLiquidity(order)
        Router->>PM: unlock(pool fill action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>Hook: tryFillOrderFromPoolLiquidity(order)
        Note over Hook,PM: Same guarded LP self-call as above, no book-priority check.
        Hook-->>Router: true if filled, false if LP attempt rolled back
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Caller: Transaction succeeds, inspect events for actual fill
    else Maker reprices
        Maker->>Hook: updatePrice(order, newAmountOutMin)
        Hook->>Match: Update minimum, re-enter with fresh sequence
        Match-->>Hook: New price and rank
        Hook-->>Maker: AsyncOrderPriceUpdated event
        Note over Maker,PM: No Router or PoolManager unlock, this does not trigger matching by itself.
    else Maker cancels
        Maker->>Router: cancelOrder(order)
        Router->>PM: unlock(cancel action)
        PM->>Router: unlockCallback(data)
        Router->>Hook: cancelOrder(order)
        Hook->>Match: Validate executor, remove open order
        Match->>PM: Burn input claims and return remaining input
        PM-->>Maker: ERC-20 refund or native claims
        Match->>PM: Settle non-refundable remaining bid to LPs or FeeVault
        Match-->>Hook: AsyncOrderCancelled event
        Hook-->>Router: Cancellation complete
        Router-->>PM: Callback complete
        PM-->>Router: Unlock complete
        Router-->>Maker: Transaction succeeds
    end
```

Signed alternatives are `Hook.updatePriceWithSig` and `Router.cancelWithSig`; a relayer can submit the maker's signature. Signature checks precede the corresponding state change or cancellation unlock. Any uncaught revert rolls back the whole transaction, including transfers and bid settlements.

### Pool setup, liquidity providers, and withdrawals

The liquidity manager below is a compatible Uniswap v4 periphery contract, not Async Swap's order Router. Its precise user-facing methods depend on the chosen periphery; the PoolManager calls shown are the common execution path. Setup and withdrawals are separate transactions from order execution.

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Operator as Pool initializer
    actor Admin as Protocol owner
    actor LP as Liquidity provider
    actor Holder as Claim holder
    participant LM as v4 liquidity manager
    participant Hook as AsyncSwap hook
    participant PM as PoolManager
    participant Native as NativeClaims
    participant Tokens as TokenClaims
    participant Vault as FeeVault
    actor Recipient

    Operator->>PM: initialize(key, sqrtPriceX96)
    PM->>Hook: beforeInitialize(...)
    Hook->>Hook: Require configured USDC and dynamic-fee pool
    Hook-->>PM: beforeInitialize selector
    PM-->>Operator: Initialized tick, Initialize event
    opt Configure minimum order size
        Admin->>Hook: setMinOrder(key, minimum)
        Hook-->>Admin: Minimum recorded
    end
    LP->>LM: Add funded liquidity in a chosen tick range
    LM->>PM: unlock(liquidity operation)
    PM->>LM: unlockCallback(data)
    LM->>PM: modifyLiquidity(key, params, hookData)
    PM->>Hook: beforeAddLiquidity(...)
    Hook-->>PM: beforeAddLiquidity selector
    PM-->>LM: Liquidity and fee deltas
    LM->>PM: Settle required token amounts
    LM-->>PM: Callback complete
    PM-->>LM: Unlock complete
    LM-->>LP: Position updated
    Note over LP,PM: Eligible positions accrue swap fees in PoolManager accounting.<br/>LPs collect through their chosen liquidity manager, no per-fill LP callback.

    Holder->>PM: approve(NativeClaims, claim ID 0, amount)
    PM-->>Holder: Claim allowance recorded
    Holder->>Native: redeem(recipient, amount)
    Native->>PM: unlock(redemption)
    PM->>Native: unlockCallback(data)
    Native->>PM: burn(holder, native claim ID 0, amount)
    Native->>PM: take(native ETH, recipient, amount)
    PM-->>Recipient: ETH payment
    Native-->>PM: Callback complete, NativeRedeemed event
    PM-->>Native: Unlock complete
    Native-->>Holder: Redemption complete

    Holder->>PM: approve(TokenClaims, currency claim ID, amount)
    PM-->>Holder: Claim allowance recorded
    Holder->>Tokens: redeem(currency, recipient, amount)
    Tokens->>PM: unlock(redemption)
    PM->>Tokens: unlockCallback(data)
    Tokens->>PM: burn(holder, currency claim ID, amount)
    Tokens->>PM: take(currency, recipient, amount)
    PM-->>Recipient: ERC-20 payment
    Tokens-->>PM: Callback complete, ClaimsRedeemed event
    PM-->>Tokens: Unlock complete
    Tokens-->>Holder: Redemption complete

    Admin->>Vault: collect(currency, recipient)
    Vault->>Hook: owner()
    Hook-->>Vault: Current protocol owner
    Vault->>PM: unlock(fee collection)
    PM->>Vault: unlockCallback(data)
    Vault->>PM: Read and burn FeeVault's currency claims
    Vault->>PM: take(currency, recipient, amount)
    PM-->>Recipient: Collected fees
    Vault-->>PM: Callback complete, FeesCollected event
    PM-->>Vault: Unlock complete
    Vault-->>Admin: Collection complete
```

Native and ERC-20 redemption require a positive amount, a nonzero recipient and a claim allowance; a failed delivery (ETH rejected, or a token refusing the recipient) reverts the redemption and restores the claims and allowance, and the holder can redeem to another recipient. Fee collection only redeems FeeVault's balances and is restricted to the current hook owner. It cannot redeem maker escrow.

Sources: [Router](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/Router.sol), [AsyncSwap](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/AsyncSwap.sol), [AsyncMatching](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol), [AsyncFiller](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol), [NativeClaims](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/NativeClaims.sol), [TokenClaims](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/TokenClaims.sol), and [FeeVault](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/src/FeeVault.sol).

# Price keys and crossing

## Price keys

Every resting order is indexed on its pool's book by a `uint128` price key computed in
`AsyncFiller._priceKey`:

| Side | Key |
|---|---|
| Buy (`isBuy`, maker escrows the numeraire) | `floor(amountIn * 1e18 / amountOutMin)` |
| Sell | `floor(amountOutMin * 1e18 / amountIn)` |

A ratio that rounds to zero maps to `1`, and a ratio above `type(uint128).max` saturates at the
maximum. The key is a truncated WAD ratio, so two orders with different exact prices can share a key.
Keys order the radix tree; they do not by themselves decide whether two orders trade.

## Crossing rule

`AsyncMatching._crosses(buyKey, sellKey, buy, sell)` decides whether a buy and a sell can trade:

* `buyKey > sellKey` is a cross and `buyKey < sellKey` is not. Truncation is monotone, so a strict
  ordering of keys always reflects a strict ordering of exact prices.
* Equal keys are decided at full precision:

```
cross  <=>  buyIn / buyOut >= sellOut / sellIn
       <=>  buyIn * sellIn >= sellOut * buyOut
       <=>  floor(buyIn * sellIn / sellOut) >= buyOut      (sellOut and buyOut are nonzero)
```

implemented as `Math.mulDiv(buy.amountIn, sell.amountIn, sell.amountOutMin) >= buy.amountOutMin`.
Orders cannot be created or updated with a zero minimum, so the divisor is never zero. With equal
keys the quotient is on the order of `buyOut`, so the division cannot overflow for escrowable
amounts.

An exact tie (`buyIn * sellIn == sellOut * buyOut`) counts as a cross and executes.

## Consequences

* Equal-key noncrossing heads no longer terminate selection when another pair is eligible.
  Each priority subtree stores its minimum exact ask or maximum exact bid. The search chooses
  the higher-priority child if its summary admits a crossing order, otherwise the other child.
  Each lookup traverses at most 128 branches without scanning or persistent cursors.
* Incoming matching chooses the highest-priority eligible opposing order at the best bucket.
  Resting-book matching chooses the highest-priority buy crossing any ask in the boundary
  bucket, then the highest-priority ask crossing that buy. This buy-first lexicographic policy
  retains fee/sequence priority among feasible pairs; it does not optimize global volume.
* Every genuine cross, including the tie, produces a non-zero match in `_matchAmounts` that pays
  each maker at least their signed minimum for the input consumed. This was checked exhaustively
  for small amounts and on randomized large near-tie pairs.
* Direct order-to-order matches swap the two escrowed inputs with no protocol fee, so rounding never
  moves value to or from the protocol.

Example of equal keys without a cross:

| Order | `amountIn` | `amountOutMin` | Key |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Buy | `3e18 + 1` | `1e18` | `3000000000000000001` |
| Sell | `1e18 - 1` | `3e18 - 2` | `3000000000000000001` |

`buyIn * sellIn` is one unit below `sellOut * buyOut`, so the pair does not cross and rests.

## Tests

`test/security/PriceKeyCrossing.t.sol`:

* `test_equalKeyNonCrossingPairDoesNotBlockMatching`
* `test_matchBookMakesNoFalseMatch`
* `test_exactTieExecutes`

## Saturation

Distinct extreme ratios collapse onto the boundary keys `1` and `type(uint128).max`. The exact
equal-key test still decides crossing correctly for them, but priority among different saturated
prices follows priority bid and then sequence rather than exact price. The ordinary bucket-width
bound does not apply to the saturated upper bucket; key `1` merges the zero and one bins.

## Historical counterexample and repaired regression

`test/security/CoarsePriceBlocking.t.sol` creates a pool with an 18-decimal asset and 6-decimal
USDC fixture at 1,000 USDC/asset, minimum order 1 USDC, and no active LP liquidity. A sell
offering `2e15 - 1` asset base units for `2_000_000` USDC base units has the same key as a
1,000 USDC/asset order, but a slightly higher exact ask. Its `100_001`-unit bid outranks the
`100_000`-unit bids of 20 honest sells. Under the previous head-only policy, twenty matching buys stopped at that blocker, and 100
retries made no progress. The Python `legacy_matching=True` mode preserves that baseline.

With exact eligibility, the same twenty buys execute against the honest sells without cancelling
or outbidding the blocker. The blocker remains open, preserving its escrow and bid. The updated
`CoarsePriceBlockingTest` asserts that outcome through the real Router/hook/PoolManager, and tests
the mirrored incoming-sell case. Generated `EligiblePythonVectors.t.sol` exercises normal prices,
both clamps, blockers on both sides, mutations, partial fills, balances and fee claims.

For ordinary buckets, human price width is `10^(assetDecimals - usdcDecimals - 18)` USDC/asset:
**0.000001 USDC/asset** for 18/6 decimals. That bounds price separation, not delay or backlog.
The repaired selector guarantees finding a crossing pair in a valid book when one exists;
successful settlement and transaction submission remain required. It does not guarantee that
every low-priority order eventually fills under continuing higher-priority arrivals.

The companion model is in the local uv4 checkout under `src/uv4/priority_protocol/`, with results
and explicit modeling boundaries in `docs/priority_protocol/`. `PriorityPythonVectors.t.sol` checks
100 independently generated Python matching cases against the real matcher;
`PriorityPythonHashes.t.sol` checks order identities and signature struct hashes.

## Maintenance, gas, and verification boundaries

`EligiblePrice.sol` compares full 512-bit cross products and stores two-word exact bounds at
priority-tree nodes. Append/remove repair the affected ancestor path. Every partial fill refreshes
the bound even if neither the coarse key nor the remaining fee changes. New storage is appended
to each price level; existing live trees would need their summaries initialized before using this
code. These local changes have not been deployed.

The protocol-controlled index work is O(128 M) for M matches. Eight is the existing per-call cap,
not a per-transaction cap. Token code and external settlement costs are outside this structural
bound. `EligibleGas.t.sol` measures composed batches through a real unlock; no numerical
worst-case gas certificate or universally optimal batch size is claimed.

The updated whitepaper is in the local `asyncswap/whitepaper` checkout. Its new section contains
integer safety and search arguments, gas curves, and the constrained parameter objective.

# AuditAgent report 1: status

Tracks [`auditagent_report_1_ae602e60-d592-45ec-92ef-891968f087f0.md`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/main/audit/auditagent_report_1_ae602e60-d592-45ec-92ef-891968f087f0.md)
(Nethermind AuditAgent, scan `ae602e60`, commit `e04668ec`), plus two findings of the same kind found
while fixing it.

| Status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Fixed** | Code changed; a regression test fails on the old code and passes on the new. |
| **Acknowledged** | Kept as is on purpose; the reason is recorded. |
| **Not fixed** | Open; needs a design decision. A recommended option is given. |

## Summary

| # | Severity | Finding | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | High | `fill` pays out while the order is still live | **Fixed** |
| 2 | High | `fillFromPoolLiquidity` pays before removing the order | **Fixed** |
| 3 | Medium | Coarse `_priceKey` buckets: a non-crossing head blocks its level | **Fixed** |
| 4 | Medium | Temporary LPs capture priority bids / divert `FeeVault` forfeits | **Fixed** |
| 5 | Medium | Filler `maxPrice` caps payment, not the input received | **Fixed** |
| 6 | Medium | Favorable partial fills weaken the remaining limit | **Fixed** |
| 7 | Medium | Custom executors can skip the priority bid | **Fixed** |
| 8 | Medium | New orders bypass a crossed backlog left by the 8-match cap | **Acknowledged** (harness) / **Fixed** (live) |
| 9 | Medium | An unreceivable ERC-20 payout blocks matching | **Fixed** |
| 10 | Medium | `updatePrice` resets `sequence`, flipping maker/taker of a crossed pair | **Fixed** |
| 11 | Low | Deleting an emptied level costs gas in its historical peak | **Fixed** |
| 12 | Low | One dust order blocks `setOrderingMode` | **Fixed** |
| R-1 | — | Router fill checks the order, pulls ERC-20, then executes | **Fixed** |
| R-2 | — | A new order is matchable before its input is settled | **Fixed** |

Every finding is now fixed or acknowledged; none is open. Policy changes made alongside: a
[minimum order and tiered priority bid](#minimum-order-and-tiered-bid), and
[priority-fee-only pools](#priority-fee-only-pools) (closes 7 and 12).

The fixes are on `main`; no deployment has been made. Storage layout and public ABI changed, so they
ship as fresh contracts, not as an upgrade.

## Fixed

### 1, 2: order state is final before any payout

An ERC-20 payout runs the token's code while the PoolManager is still unlocked, and the hook's own
entry points (`cancelOrder` by the owner, `matchBook`, `updatePrice`, `executeOrder` by an executor)
are callable from there. The order must already be closed or reduced when that code runs.

* `AsyncFiller.fill`: the order is removed, deleted and its paid bid settled (`_closeOrder`) before
  the maker's output, the fee and the filler's input are paid.
* `AsyncMatching.fillFromPoolLiquidity`: the order is removed and deleted before the pool swap and the
  maker's payout.
* `AsyncMatching._matchPair`: recipients are read first (`_payouts`), both orders are reduced, then
  the two escrow legs pay out (`_settleTransfers`). Since the fix for 9, those legs credit PoolManager
  claims and run no token code at all.

Tests: `test/nethermind_auditagent/NethermindAuditAgent.t.sol`
`test_H1_fill_orderClosedBeforeMakerPayout`, `test_H2_poolLiquidityFill_orderClosedBeforeMakerPayout`
(a token notifies the paid maker, which only reads the order's record) and
`test_H1_match_orderReducedBeforeMakerPayout` (the match credits claims and the token's code never runs).

### 3: exact eligibility inside coarse price buckets

`EligiblePrice` augments each priority radix tree with exact subtree price extrema. A lookup
returns the highest-fee, earliest-sequence order that crosses the counterparty in at most 128
branches. Noncrossing heads remain open and no longer hide eligible lower-priority orders.
For a resting equal-key book, selection maximizes buy priority first, then eligible sell priority.
Append/remove and every live partial fill maintain the extrema, including unchanged-key/fee fills.

The original approximately 2-USDC blocker no longer stalls 20,000 USDC of executable orders.
`CoarsePriceBlockingTest` covers both incoming directions. `EligiblePythonVectors.t.sol` compares
514 operations and 132 matches against an independent rational-price Python oracle, including
both clamps, two-sided blockers, mutations, selected IDs, remainders, fees, and maker balances.
`EligiblePriceTest` checks subtree invariants, randomized mutations, full depth, and node reuse.

The index bound is independent of blocker count. Matching runs no token code (finding 9), so a
blocker cannot make it revert or burn gas through a payout. See `docs/price-key-crossing.md` and the
revised whitepaper for the argument.

### 4: priority bids always go to the `FeeVault`

`AsyncFiller.settlePriorityFee` no longer checks in-range liquidity: every settled bid (the filled
share on a match, the rest on close, cancel, fill or pool fill) is burned from the hook's claims and
minted to the `FeeVault`. Liquidity added for the moment of settlement receives none of it. (Active
LPs still earn the 30 bps fill fee on a pool fill, as on any Uniswap swap; that fee is not a bid.)

Tests: `test_M4_liquidityAddedBeforeFillGetsNoBid` (on the audited code the bid shows up as LP fee
growth), `test_filledPriorityBidGoesToFeeVaultNotActiveLps`, `test_lpCollectsFillFeeOnWithdraw`.

### 5: `order.amountIn` bounds what the filler receives

`Router.unlockCallback` (fill) reverts with `"Input below order.amountIn"` when the order's live input
is below `order.amountIn`. A missing order (live input 0) still reaches the hook's `OrderNotFound`.

Tests: `test_M5_RevertWhen_LiveInputBelowFillerExpectation`, `test_M5_fillSucceeds_WhenFillerAcceptsLiveInput`.

### 6: the remainder keeps the maker's own limit

`AsyncMatching._reduceAfterMatch` sets the remaining minimum to
`ceil(oldMinimum * remainingInput / oldInput)` instead of `oldMinimum - outputReceived`. A side
closes only when its input is used up; the early close-and-refund branch is gone.

**Behavior change:** an order that fills at a better price than its limit now keeps its unspent
input on the book at its own limit, where it used to be refunded. Three existing tests were updated:
`test_crossingOrdersMatchAndTransferEscrowedTokens`, `test_priorityFeeBreaksEqualPriceTiesAfterPricePriority`
(`test/AsyncSwap.t.sol`), `test_retryFillsPartiallyMatchedRemainder` (`test/PoolLiquidityFill.t.sol`).

Tests: `test_M6_favorablePartialFill_keepsRemainderLimit`, `test_M6_favorablePartialFill_keepsBuyerRemainderLimit`,
`test_M6_partialFillMeetingWholeMinimum_keepsRemainderResting`.

### 8 (live): one book-wide priority for arrivals and backlog

`AsyncMatching.matchIncoming` now runs `matchBook` on the whole book, within the same 8-match budget,
instead of matching only the new order against the best opposing level. A crossed backlog left by
the cap clears first, by price, then bid, then time; the new order takes its place in that queue.

Test: `test_M8_crossedBacklogClearsBeforeNewerOrder` (on the audited code a newer, worse-priced ask
fills while the older crossed ask stays on the book).

### 9: match payouts are claims

`AsyncMatching._transferEscrow` credits ERC-6909 claims in every currency, for both escrow legs and
for a remainder returned below the pool minimum. Holders redeem with the new `TokenClaims`
(`redeem(currency, recipient, amount)`, after approving it on the PoolManager), to any recipient the
token accepts. A recipient the token refuses therefore cannot revert a match.

Fills by a filler and pool-liquidity fills still pay the maker in ERC-20. A refused maker can only
fail its own order there: the pool fill runs behind a caught self-call and leaves the order resting,
and a filler fill reverts for that one order.

Tests: `test_M9_blockedRecipientDoesNotBlockMatch` (on the audited code the refused transfer reverts
the whole match), `test/TokenClaims.t.sol` (redemption, approvals, a refused transfer restoring claims
and allowance, re-entry).

### 10: the maker role survives a reprice

Each order now records an immutable `createdSequence`. `_matchPair` makes the order with the smaller
`createdSequence` the maker, whose limit sets the price. `updatePrice` still takes a fresh `sequence`,
which only sets queue position among equal-price, equal-bid orders.

Test: `test_M10_repriceKeepsMakerRole` (on the audited code the older buy's reprice flips the maker,
and the seller receives 11 instead of 12).

The regression tests for 4, 8, 9 and 10 were run against the audited commit `e04668e` with the current
`SetupHook` and its pools switched to priority-fee mode: each fails there on its own assertion and
passes on `main`.

### 11: an emptied price level is left in place

`AsyncFiller._remove` no longer deletes the `PriceLevel` when its last order leaves. Its FIFO links
are already zero and its priority tree is empty (root 0); deleting it only cleared the tree's
`nextNodeId` and `freeIds`, a cost that grew with the level's historical peak. Those ids are now
reused by later orders at that price.

Tests: no dedicated gas test.

### R-1: the Router fills only the order it checked

Found while fixing 1 and 2. The fill path read the order (live input, price, `maxPrice`), then pulled
the filler's ERC-20 with `safeTransferFrom`, which runs the token's code, then executed against
whatever storage held by then. A changed price already reverted (the hook's deltas no longer net to
zero); a reduced input did not. `Router` now re-reads the order after the pull and reverts with
`"Order changed during fill"` unless it is unchanged (`_requireUnchanged`).

Test: `test/security/RouterOrderWindow.t.sol` `test_RevertWhen_OrderChangesDuringFillPayment`.

### R-2: a new order is not matchable before its input is settled

Found while fixing 1 and 2. `_beforeSwap` puts the order on the book before the Router pulls the
maker's input and priority bid, and the Router's comment said it "only becomes matchable after this
maker's input has been settled". The permissionless `matchBook` did not enforce that. It now returns 0
while this pool holds the order pending in `PENDING_MATCH_ID_SLOT`, i.e. until `matchNewOrder` takes
it. An early match also needed the PoolManager to hold the token from other escrow or LP reserves.

Test: `test/security/RouterOrderWindow.t.sol` `test_pendingOrder_notMatchableBeforeInputSettled`.

## Minimum order and tiered bid

Async Swap targets institutional-size orders; small trades are better served by the AMM. Measured in
numeraire (USDC) base units:

* **Minimum order.** Each pool has a minimum (`setMinOrder(key, amount)`, owner only); pools start with
  the hook's `defaultMinOrder` (`setDefaultMinOrder`). `script/01_DeployHook.s.sol` sets it to $10
  (`DEPLOY_MIN_ORDER_USD`, scaled by the numeraire's `decimals()`). A buy's input must be at least the
  minimum; a sell's minimum output must be, and so must its input valued at the pool's current price,
  which keeps out sells that ask for the minimum but offer almost nothing. `updatePrice` re-checks it.
  The pool price is an estimate: an empty pool still shows its creation price, so this is an admission
  gate, not an oracle.
* **Remainders.** A partial match that leaves an order worth less than the minimum, by its own terms
  (no pool price), closes it and returns the remaining input as claims after both orders are reduced.
* **Tiered bid.** The least bid is `min($0.10, 0.1% of the order)`: $0.10 from $100 up, down to $0.01
  at the $10 minimum.

Tests: `test/security/MinimumOrder.t.sol`, including a sell and a buy remainder refunded below the
minimum, and the value check on a pool whose numeraire is `currency0`. Formal tests updated: the `addOrder` and `CreateOrderSpec`
fee guards, and `beforeInitialize`'s write set (now also `priceBooks[id].minOrder`).

Hook size: `updatePriceWithSig` called the internal `AsyncFiller.updatePrice`, inlining it into the
hook; it now goes through the linked `AsyncMatching.updatePrice` like `updatePrice`. `AsyncSwap` went
from 24,311 to about 20,200 bytes (EIP-170 limit 24,576).

## Priority-fee-only pools

Findings **7 and 12 are fixed** in the working tree. Every pool queues equal-price orders by
escrowed bid, then sequence. FIFO mode, its links, `setOrderingMode`, `orderingMode`, and the separate
`recordPriorityFee` call are removed. `orderBookOrder` now returns `sequence` and `priorityFee` in
its final two fields instead of FIFO neighbors; clients must update their ABI.

`addOrder` mints the bid's numeraire claims to the hook immediately. This creates a matching hook
debt in PoolManager; the unlock cannot finish until it is settled. The Router pays it with
`settleFor(hook)`. A custom executor cannot leave an order resting with an unpaid declared bid.
The tiered minimum still rounds down in base units, so a tiny order can have a zero minimum when
the pool minimum permits it. This change does not impose a universal $10 minimum.

Tests: `test/security/PriorityFeeOnly.t.sol` checks minimum bids on unconfigured pools, bid ordering,
rejection of an executor that skips payment, successful paid custom execution, equal-bid time ordering,
and removal of the mode setter. Existing placement,
settlement, cancellation and invariant fixtures now account for escrowed bids.

This changes storage layout and public ABI; deploy fresh contracts and update consumers. It is not
a migration of existing orders or deployed contracts.

## Acknowledged

### 8 (harness): `MatchingEngine`

`src/MatchingEngine.sol` is a standalone matching harness and gas benchmark; it holds no tokens.

## Running the tests

```sh
forge test --match-path "test/nethermind_auditagent/*"
forge test --match-contract RouterOrderWindowTest
forge test                                   # everything
```

## Validation

* `forge test`: **833 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped** across 139 suites. The Unichain fork fixture skips
  without `UNICHAIN_FORK_RPC_URL`; no fork validation is claimed.
* `forge build --sizes`: runtime sizes are 19,237 bytes (`AsyncSwap`), 19,064 bytes (`AsyncMatching`)
  and 17,580 bytes (`Router`), each below the 24,576-byte EIP-170 limit.
* `forge coverage` of `src/`: 99.9% of lines, 99.4% of statements, 98.8% of branches, 100% of
  functions. The uncovered branches are unreachable guards (a matched amount above the order's input,
  `MatchingEngine`'s reentrancy check, a sell-only lookup).
* No deployment was performed.

# Contract reference

These pages are generated by `forge doc` from the NatSpec comments in
[`src/`](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/tree/main/src) on every docs build, so they always
match the code on `main`. Each page links to its source file.

| Contract | Role |
| --- | --- |
| [AsyncSwap](/reference/src/AsyncSwap) | The Uniswap v4 hook: turns swaps into orders, escrows input and bids, entry point for matching, fills and cancels. |
| [Router](/reference/src/Router) | Entry point for makers, fillers and relayers: `swap`, `fillOrder`, `cancelOrder`, signed variants, `matchBook`, `fillFromPoolLiquidity`. |
| [AsyncMatching](/reference/src/libraries/AsyncMatching) | Linked library that matches the book, fills from pool liquidity and settles each pair. |
| [AsyncFiller](/reference/src/libraries/AsyncFiller) | Order storage and the per-pool book: placement, fills, cancels, repricing, bid settlement. |
| [FeeVault](/reference/src/FeeVault) | Holds protocol fee and bid claims; the owner collects them. |
| [TokenClaims](/reference/src/TokenClaims) | Redeems ERC-20 PoolManager claims, such as match proceeds, to any recipient. |
| [NativeClaims](/reference/src/NativeClaims) | Redeems native ETH claims to any recipient. |
| [RadixPriceTree](/reference/src/libraries/RadixPriceTree) and [EligiblePrice](/reference/src/libraries/EligiblePrice) | The price index and the exact-price summaries that find the best crossing order. |

`MatchingEngine` is a standalone benchmark harness and is not deployed.

# AsyncSwap

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/AsyncSwap.sol)

**Inherits:** [BaseHook](/reference/src/BaseHook), EIP712

**Title:** AsyncSwap

**Author:** @msakiart

Uniswap v4 hook that converts an exact-input swap into an open async order: the maker
deposits their input via `_beforeSwap`. Crossing orders settle directly at the resting
limit; fillers settle unmatched orders.

Makers can also act by EIP-712 signature (`setExecutorWithSig`, `updatePriceWithSig`) so a
relayer pays gas and the wallet shows a readable message. See `OrderSignatures` for types.

## Constants

### feeVault

Holds fee claims separately from open-order escrow.

```solidity
FeeVault public immutable feeVault;
```

### numeraire

Chain-specific USDC address. Every pool must include this exact currency.

```solidity
Currency public immutable numeraire;
```

### PENDING_NATIVE_DEPOSIT_SLOT

<i>
  Transient slot — keccak256("asyncswap.hook.pendingNativeDeposit") - 1.
  Tracks ETH deposited to this contract within the current tx via
  `receive()`, so `executeOrder` can settle native output only out of
  the filler's just-received deposit rather than the contract's
  accumulated balance (which may include donations, stranded ETH,
  or in-flight native-input escrow). Cleared after each settle.
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 constant PENDING_NATIVE_DEPOSIT_SLOT = 0x9c2a7e4f3b1d8a5c6e0f2d4b7a9c1e3d5f8b6a0c2e4d7b9f1a3c5e7d9b1f3a50;
```

### PENDING_MATCH_ID_SLOT

<i>
  Transient hand-off from `_beforeSwap` to the Router after it settles the new input.
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 constant PENDING_MATCH_ID_SLOT = 0x247d5e35be7fbfd4d95fd66ea940bfb4ee942bef70db6afae46dc83ce0f89eb2;
```

### PENDING_MATCH_EXECUTOR_SLOT

```solidity
bytes32 constant PENDING_MATCH_EXECUTOR_SLOT = 0x9583e36f799bab8c4d06dc676d85ba05b4dfbde5934d5684d8e431d0fd3948da;
```

Protocol owner authorized to collect vault fees and sweep stranded balances.

Address nominated by `transferOwnership`; becomes owner on `acceptOwnership`.

```solidity

```

Unordered nonces consumed by signed maker actions (`setExecutorWithSig`, `updatePriceWithSig`).

```solidity

```

### defaultMinOrder

Minimum order, in numeraire base units, that pools initialized from now on start with.

```solidity

```

<a id="sweep-currency-address" />

### sweep

Sweep an accumulated balance of `currency` held by this hook to `to`.

<i>
  Between transactions the hook's raw balance holds only stranded funds or donations;
  fees belong to feeVault. Maker input is escrowed as ERC-6909
  claims in the PoolManager, and the transient native-deposit ledger is cleared at the
  end of every tx, so no per-order escrow lives in the hook's balance across calls.
</i>

```solidity
function sweep(Currency currency, address to) external onlyOwner;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| currency | `Currency` |  |
| to | `address` |  |

<a id="receive" />

### receive

Accept ETH transfers. The Router (or any caller paying for a native-output
fill) forwards `msg.value` to the hook before triggering `executeOrder`. The hook
records the deposit on a transient slot so `executeOrder` settles only against the
filler's same-transaction deposit. ETH sent without a follow-up `executeOrder` stays
in the hook balance and is recoverable only through `sweep`.

```solidity
receive() external payable;
```

## Events

### HookSwap

Pool-level swap-event mirror; bytes32 poolId for indexer compatibility.

<i>
  See https://github.com/OpenZeppelin/uniswap-hooks BaseAsyncSwap for the source pattern.
</i>

```solidity
event HookSwap(
        bytes32 indexed id,
        address indexed sender,
        int128 amount0,
        int128 amount1,
        uint128 hookLPfeeAmount0,
        uint128 hookLPfeeAmount1
    );
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

## Structs

### UserParams

Hook params decoded from the `hookData` of `IPoolManager.swap`. The maker sets
`amountOutMin` (their limit price); `executor` is the address authorized to call fill.
Salt is contract-assigned at create time (see `_createOrder`) and emitted in
`AsyncOrderCreated` — the maker fetches it from the event log to reference the
order in cancel / updatePrice later.

```solidity
struct UserParams {
        address user;
        address executor;
        uint256 amountOutMin;
        uint256 priorityFee;
    }
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| user | `address` |  |
| executor | `address` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |
| priorityFee | `uint256` |  |

# MatchingEngine

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/MatchingEngine.sol)

**Title:** MatchingEngine

Standalone price-time matching harness. It maintains a radix-indexed
limit book and emits deterministic fill instructions.

<i>
  Algorithm and gas benchmark only: it does not custody or settle tokens.
  Live orders settle through the AsyncSwap hook and AsyncMatching.
</i>

Submit a limit order. Crossing orders match immediately, up to

# Router

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/Router.sol)

**Inherits:** EIP712

**Title:** Router

**Author:** @msakiart

Thin entrypoint for makers (`swap`), fillers (`fillOrder`), and makers cancelling orders
(`cancelOrder`). All three actions go through `IPoolManager.unlock` so the hook can
operate on PM debts. Native payouts/refunds are PoolManager claims (ID 0),
redeemable through NativeClaims after approval; ERC20 payouts remain direct.

Gasless variants (`swapWithSig`, `cancelWithSig`) take the maker's EIP-712 signature so a
relayer can submit. Signed creates pull input through Permit2 with the order as witness,
so the wallet shows the full order (tokens, amounts, pool) in one readable message.

## Constants

### POOLMANAGER

```solidity
IPoolManager immutable POOLMANAGER;
```

### HOOK

```solidity
AsyncSwap immutable HOOK;
```

### PERMIT2

```solidity
ISignatureTransfer public immutable PERMIT2;
```

### ACTION_LOCATION

keccak256("Router.ActionType") - 1

```solidity
bytes32 constant ACTION_LOCATION = 0xf3b150ebf41dad0872df6788629edb438733cb4a5c9ea779b1b1f3614faffc69;
```

### USER_LOCATION

keccak256("Router.User") - 1

```solidity
bytes32 constant USER_LOCATION = 0x3dde20d9bf5cc25a9f487c6d6b54d3c19e3fa4738b91a7a509d4fc4180a72356;
```

### ASYNC_FILLER_LOCATION

keccak256("Router.AsyncFiller") - 1

```solidity
bytes32 constant ASYNC_FILLER_LOCATION = 0xd972a937b59dc5cb8c692dd9f211e85afa8def4caee6e05b31db0f53e16d02e0;
```

### MAX_PRICE_LOCATION

<i>
  keccak256("asyncswap.router.maxPrice") - 1
</i>

```solidity
bytes32 constant MAX_PRICE_LOCATION = 0x6b4f8e2c9d5a0b7e1f3c2a8d4e9f0b6c5a1d8e7f2b3c4d5e6a7f8b9c0d1e2f30;
```

## State Variables


## Functions

<a id="onlypoolmanager" />

### onlyPoolManager

```solidity
modifier onlyPoolManager();
```

<a id="swap-asyncorder-bytes" />

### swap

Maker submits a new async order. `userData` must encode `AsyncSwap.UserParams`
with `executor == address(this)` so the router is authorized to fill later.
`userData.amountOutMin` MUST equal `order.amountOutMin` — the router enforces
this so the limit price the maker signs in `order` is exactly what beforeSwap
stores via hookData.

The hook auto-assigns a salt on create and emits it in `AsyncOrderCreated`.
Submitters can pass `order.salt = bytes32(0)` on initial submission; the
field is only read on cancel / updatePrice / fill paths (where the maker
supplies the salt fetched from the indexer or event log).

Native input (currency0 = address(0) and zeroForOne = true, OR currency1 =
address(0) and zeroForOne = false) requires `msg.value == order.amountIn` —
the router holds the ETH and settles it to PM during unlock. For ERC20 input
the maker must approve the router for `amountIn` of the input token.

```solidity
function swap(AsyncOrder calldata order, bytes memory userData) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| userData | `bytes` |  |

<a id="fillorder-asyncorder-uint256-bytes" />

### fillOrder

Filler completes an open order, paying the maker's net minimum plus the protocol fee.
For ERC20 output, approve the router for that gross amount. For native output,
`msg.value` must equal the live net price plus the protocol fee;
a stale or excessive deposit reverts rather than stranding the difference.
Native output is currency1 for zeroForOne, otherwise currency0.

`maxPrice` caps total output paid, including the fee —
it protects fillers from a maker who front-runs them with `updatePrice` to
bump the order's stored price. Pass `type(uint256).max` to disable the check.
`order.amountIn` is the least input the filler accepts: the fill reverts if the
order's live input has dropped below it (e.g. after a partial match).

```solidity
function fillOrder(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 maxPrice, bytes calldata) external payable;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| maxPrice | `uint256` |  |
| \_ | `bytes` |  |

<a id="swapwithsig-asyncorder-permitdata-executorgrant" />

### swapWithSig

Relayer submits a maker's signed order. The maker signs a Permit2
`PermitWitnessTransferFrom` for `amountIn` of the input token with `spender = Router`
and the `AsyncOrder` witness (see `OrderSignatures`), so one signature both approves
the transfer and commits to the order. Input then lands in the hook escrow exactly as
in `swap`. Requires a prior Permit2 approval of the input token; native input is not
supported (use `swap`).

```solidity
function swapWithSig(AsyncOrder calldata order, PermitData calldata permit, ExecutorGrant calldata grant) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| permit | `PermitData` |  |
| grant | `ExecutorGrant` |  |

<a id="cancelwithsig-asyncorder-uint256-uint256-bytes" />

### cancelWithSig

Relayer submits a maker's signed EIP-712 `CancelOrder`. Input returns to the maker.

```solidity
function cancelWithSig(AsyncOrder calldata order, uint256 nonce, uint256 deadline, bytes calldata signature)
        external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| nonce | `uint256` |  |
| deadline | `uint256` |  |
| signature | `bytes` |  |

<a id="domain_separator" />

### DOMAIN_SEPARATOR


| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

<a id="matchbook-poolkey-uint8" />

### matchBook

Anyone can continue a crossed book after a transaction hits the automatic match cap.

<i>
  Work is capped at eight matched pairs per unlock to keep gas predictable.
</i>

```solidity
function matchBook(PoolKey calldata key, uint8 maxMatches) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| key | `PoolKey` |  |
| maxMatches | `uint8` |  |

<a id="fillfrompoolliquidity-asyncorder" />

### fillFromPoolLiquidity

Retry a resting order against the pool's active Uniswap v4 LP positions.

<i>
  The order is left untouched when the pool cannot fully fill it at its minimum output.
</i>

```solidity
function fillFromPoolLiquidity(AsyncOrder calldata order) external;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

<a id="_settlewithpermit-currency-asyncorder-permitdata" />

### \_settleWithPermit

<i>
  Pays the maker's input into the PoolManager via Permit2. Permit2 verifies the maker's
  signature over the transfer AND the order witness, so a relayer cannot alter the order.
</i>

```solidity
function _settleWithPermit(Currency input, AsyncOrder memory order, PermitData memory permit) private;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| input | `Currency` |  |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| permit | `PermitData` |  |

<a id="_settlepriorityfee-asyncorder" />

### \_settlePriorityFee

<i>
  Pays the order's bid, which the hook escrowed as claims when it created the order, in the
  pool's USDC numeraire. Signed orders also require an ERC-20 approval for the bid; the
  signed order commits to its amount.
</i>

```solidity
function _settlePriorityFee(AsyncOrder memory order) private;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

# TokenClaims

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/TokenClaims.sol)

Redeems the caller's PoolManager currency claims to a chosen recipient.

<i>
  Approve this contract for the currency claim ID on PoolManager before redeeming.
  Claim ownership and allowances are enforced by PoolManager.burn. No hook escrow is accessible.
</i>

## Constants

### poolManager

```solidity
IPoolManager public immutable poolManager;
```

<a id="afteraddliquidity-address-poolkey-modifyliquidityparams-balancedelta-balancedelta-bytes" />

### afterAddLiquidity

The hook called after liquidity is added

```solidity
function afterAddLiquidity(
        address sender,
        PoolKey calldata key,
        ModifyLiquidityParams calldata params,
        BalanceDelta delta,
        BalanceDelta feesAccrued,
        bytes calldata hookData
    ) external onlyPoolManager returns (bytes4, BalanceDelta);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| sender | `address` | The initial msg.sender for the add liquidity call |
| key | `PoolKey` | The key for the pool |
| params | `ModifyLiquidityParams` | The parameters for adding liquidity |
| delta | `BalanceDelta` | The caller's balance delta after adding liquidity; the sum of principal delta, fees accrued, and hook delta |
| feesAccrued | `BalanceDelta` | The fees accrued since the last time fees were collected from this position |
| hookData | `bytes` | Arbitrary data handed into the PoolManager by the liquidity provider to be passed on to the hook |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes4` | bytes4 The function selector for the hook |
| \<none> | `BalanceDelta` | BalanceDelta The hook's delta in token0 and token1. Positive: the hook is owed/took currency, negative: the hook owes/sent currency |

<a id="_afteraddliquidity-address-poolkey-modifyliquidityparams-balancedelta-balancedelta-bytes" />

<a id="beforeswap-address-poolkey-swapparams-bytes" />

### beforeSwap

The hook called before a swap

```solidity
function beforeSwap(address sender, PoolKey calldata key, SwapParams calldata params, bytes calldata hookData)
        external
        onlyPoolManager
        returns (bytes4, BeforeSwapDelta, uint24);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| sender | `address` | The initial msg.sender for the swap call |
| key | `PoolKey` | The key for the pool |
| params | `SwapParams` | The parameters for the swap |
| hookData | `bytes` | Arbitrary data handed into the PoolManager by the swapper to be be passed on to the hook |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes4` | bytes4 The function selector for the hook |
| \<none> | `BeforeSwapDelta` | BeforeSwapDelta The hook's delta in specified and unspecified currencies. Positive: the hook is owed/took currency, negative: the hook owes/sent currency |
| \<none> | `uint24` | uint24 Optionally override the lp fee, only used if three conditions are met: 1. the Pool has a dynamic fee, 2. the value's 2nd highest bit is set (23rd bit, 0x400000), and 3. the value is less than or equal to the maximum fee (1 million) |

# ISignatureTransfer

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/interfaces/ISignatureTransfer.sol)

**Title:** ISignatureTransfer

Minimal subset of Uniswap Permit2's SignatureTransfer interface used by the Router.
Canonical Permit2 lives at 0x000000000022D473030F116dDEE9F6B43aC78BA3 on every chain.

<i>
  Vendored instead of imported because Permit2's sources pin solc 0.8.17.
</i>

# AsyncFiller

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/libraries/AsyncFiller.sol)

**Title:** AsyncFiller

**Author:** @msakiart

Stores open async orders and settles fills against them.

<i>
  Authorization model: the maker authorizes a Router/executor at order-creation time
  (`setExecutor[owner][executor] = true`). All subsequent fill / cancel / updatePrice
  calls on the hook must come from that registered executor. The hook forwards its
  immediate caller (`msg.sender`) and the resolved end-actor address (filler / canceller)
  into this library; the executor is checked here, and PM settlement targets the actor.
</i>

## Constants

### PRICE_SCALE

```solidity
uint256 private constant PRICE_SCALE = 1e18;
```

### MAX_PRIORITY_FEE

```solidity
uint64 internal constant MAX_PRIORITY_FEE = type(uint64).max;
```

### MIN_PRIORITY_FEE

<i>
  $0.10 in six-decimal USDC base units. Async Swap pools are configured with USDC as numeraire.
</i>

```solidity
uint64 internal constant MIN_PRIORITY_FEE = 100_000;
```

### PRIORITY_FEE_BPS

<i>
  Below a $100 order the least bid is 10 bps of the order instead: min($0.10, 0.1% of it).
</i>

```solidity
uint256 internal constant PRIORITY_FEE_BPS = 10;
```

<a id="checkminimum-state-book-poolid-bool-bool-uint256-uint256" />

### checkMinimum

Reverts unless the order is worth at least the pool's minimum in the numeraire: a buy's
input; a sell's minimum output and its input at the pool's current price. The price
check keeps out sells that ask for the minimum but offer almost nothing.

```solidity
function checkMinimum(
        State storage self,
        Book storage book,
        PoolId poolId,
        bool isBuy,
        bool zeroForOne,
        uint256 amountIn,
        uint256 amountOutMin
    ) internal view;
```

<a id="fill-state-book-asyncorder-bytes32-address-address-address-address-uint256" />

### fill

Full-fill. The caller (the hook contract) must be an authorized executor of the
order owner; `filler` is the actual end-user paying the output and receiving the
input. Must be invoked from inside an `IPoolManager.unlock` context.

<i>
  Settle gross output (native only; ERC20 is pre-settled), pay the signed net minimum to the maker, and mint fee
  claims to the vault. Burn input claims and pay the full input to the filler.
  Both currency deltas net to zero. A failed fill reverts all legs.
</i>

```solidity
function fill(
        State storage self,
        Book storage book,
        AsyncOrder memory order,
        bytes32 id,
        address hook,
        address executor,
        address filler,
        address feeVault,
        uint256 fee
    ) internal;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `State` |  |
| book | `Book` |  |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |
| id | `bytes32` |  |
| hook | `address` |  |
| executor | `address` |  |
| filler | `address` |  |
| feeVault | `address` |  |
| fee | `uint256` |  |
