<a id="cancel-state-book-asyncorder-bytes32-address-address" />

### cancel

Cancel an unfilled order. Must be called inside an unlock context. Auth: `executor`
must be either the order owner themselves (smart-contract makers calling the hook
directly from their own unlock) or an executor the maker authorised via
`setExecutor`. Funds always return to `order.owner`.

```solidity
function cancel(
        State storage self,
        Book storage book,
        AsyncOrder memory order,
        bytes32 id,
        address hook,
        address executor
    ) internal;
```

**Parameters**

## Structs

### OrderInfo

Open-order record. Filler fills are full-order; direct matches can reduce it
partially while keeping the remaining input in escrow.

```solidity
struct OrderInfo {
        address owner;
        uint256 amountIn;
        uint256 amountOutMin;
        uint128 price;
        bool isBuy;
        bool zeroForOne;
        uint64 sequence;
        /// @dev The bid, escrowed as hook claims since the order was created.
        uint64 priorityFee;
        uint128 priorityKey;
        /// @dev Immutable settlement age; repricing only resets queue sequence.
        uint64 createdSequence;
    }
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| owner | `address` |  |
| amountIn | `uint256` |  |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` |  |
| price | `uint128` |  |
| isBuy | `bool` |  |
| zeroForOne | `bool` |  |
| sequence | `uint64` |  |
| priorityFee | `uint64` |  |
| priorityKey | `uint128` |  |
| createdSequence | `uint64` |  |

### PriceLevel

<i>
  Orders at one price, highest bid first, then earliest.

```solidity
        mapping(uint32 nodeId => EligiblePrice.Ratio) exactBounds;
    }
```

| Name | Type | Description |

```solidity
struct Book {
```

# AsyncMatching

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/libraries/AsyncMatching.sol)

Linked matching module operating on the hook's order and radix-book storage.

<i>
  Public library calls use DELEGATECALL, so ERC-6909 escrow remains owned by Async Swap.
</i>

## Constants

### PRICE_SCALE

```solidity
uint256 private constant PRICE_SCALE = 1e18;
```

### MAX_MATCHES_PER_CALL

```solidity
uint8 public constant MAX_MATCHES_PER_CALL = 8;
```

### POOL_LIQUIDITY_FILL_FEE

```solidity
uint24 private constant POOL_LIQUIDITY_FILL_FEE = 3_000;
```

## Functions

<a id="addorder-asyncfiller-state-asyncfiller-book-asyncfiller-neworder" />

### addOrder

```solidity

        public;
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `AsyncFiller.State` |  |
| book | `AsyncFiller.Book` |  |
| order | `AsyncFiller.NewOrder` |  |

<a id="_crosses-uint128-uint128-asyncfiller-orderinfo-asyncfiller-orderinfo" />

### \_crosses

Decide whether a buy and a sell order cross, i.e. a price exists that satisfies both
makers' limits.

<i>
  The `uint128` price keys on the book are truncated WAD ratios, so two distinct prices
  can share a key. Strictly ordered keys decide the result directly, since truncation
  cannot invert a strict inequality. Equal keys are decided by a full-precision
  cross-multiply:
</i>

cross  \<=>  buyIn/buyOut >= sellOut/sellIn  \<=>  buyIn*sellIn >= sellOut*buyOut
\<=>  floor(buyIn\*sellIn / sellOut) >= buyOut   (sellOut, buyOut are nonzero).

An exact tie counts as a cross. With equal keys the quotient is on the order of
`buyOut`, so the `mulDiv` cannot overflow for escrowable amounts.

```solidity
function _crosses(
        uint128 buyKey,
        uint128 sellKey,
        AsyncFiller.OrderInfo storage buy,
        AsyncFiller.OrderInfo storage sell
    ) internal view returns (bool);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| buyKey | `uint128` |  |
| sellKey | `uint128` |  |
| buy | `AsyncFiller.OrderInfo` |  |
| sell | `AsyncFiller.OrderInfo` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bool` |  |

# CurrencySettler

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/libraries/CurrencySettler.sol)

**Title:** CurrencySettler

Production copy of v4-core's test-only `CurrencySettler`, using safe transfers so tokens
that return no data from `transfer` / `transferFrom` (e.g. USDT) settle correctly.

# EligiblePrice

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/libraries/EligiblePrice.sol)

Exact-price summaries on a priority-key radix tree.

<i>
  A buy subtree stores its maximum limit; a sell subtree its minimum.
  This is an existence certificate, not an approximation of an order's limit.
</i>

## Functions

<a id="le-ratio-ratio" />

<i>
  Exact comparison of positive-denominator ratios using two 512-bit products.
</i>


| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

<a id="best-radixpricetree-tree-mapping-uint32-ratio-ratio-bool" />

### best

Highest priority key among orders crossing `limit`, in at most 128 branches.

<i>
  Right children have greater priority keys. No backtracking or linear scan.
</i>

```solidity
        mapping(uint32 => Ratio) storage bounds,
        Ratio memory limit,
        bool isBuy
    ) internal view returns (bool found, uint128 rank);
```

# OrderSignatures

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/libraries/OrderSignatures.sol)

**Title:** OrderSignatures

**Author:** @msakiart

EIP-712 types for signed AsyncSwap actions. Every type spells out the maker, both tokens
and the amounts so wallets render a readable message instead of opaque calldata.

* `AsyncOrder` is the Permit2 witness for `Router.swapWithSig` (Permit2 domain).
* `SetExecutor` and `UpdatePrice` are verified by the hook (AsyncSwap domain).
* `CancelOrder` is verified by the Router (AsyncSwap Router domain).

## Constants

### POOL_KEY_TYPE

```solidity
bytes internal constant POOL_KEY_TYPE =
        "PoolKey(address currency0,address currency1,uint24 fee,int24 tickSpacing,address hooks)";
```

### ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE

```solidity
bytes internal constant ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE =
        "AsyncOrder(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,uint256 amountOutMin,uint256 priorityFee,PoolKey pool)";
```

### POOL_KEY_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant POOL_KEY_TYPEHASH = keccak256(POOL_KEY_TYPE);
```

### ASYNC_ORDER_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant ASYNC_ORDER_TYPEHASH = keccak256(abi.encodePacked(ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE, POOL_KEY_TYPE));
```

### PERMIT2_WITNESS_TYPE

Witness type string appended by Permit2 to `PermitWitnessTransferFrom(...)`.
Referenced types are sorted alphabetically per EIP-712.

```solidity
string internal constant PERMIT2_WITNESS_TYPE = string(
        abi.encodePacked(
            "AsyncOrder witness)", ASYNC_ORDER_TYPE, POOL_KEY_TYPE, "TokenPermissions(address token,uint256 amount)"
        )
    );
```

### SET_EXECUTOR_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant SET_EXECUTOR_TYPEHASH = keccak256(
        abi.encodePacked(
            "SetExecutor(address maker,address executor,bool allow,PoolKey pool,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)",
            POOL_KEY_TYPE
        )
    );
```

### UPDATE_PRICE_TYPEHASH

```solidity
bytes32 internal constant UPDATE_PRICE_TYPEHASH = keccak256(
        "UpdatePrice(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,uint256 newAmountOutMin,bytes32 orderId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)"
    );
```

### CANCEL_ORDER_TYPEHASH

```solidity
        "CancelOrder(address maker,address tokenIn,address tokenOut,uint256 amountIn,bytes32 orderId,uint256 nonce,uint256 deadline)"
    );
```

### hashOrder

Struct hash of the order a maker signs as the Permit2 witness. Covers everything that

# RadixPriceTree

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/libraries/RadixPriceTree.sol)

Patricia radix index for uint128 price levels. Inserts and removals
traverse at most 128 branch bits; each distinct price creates one
leaf and at most one branch node. Node ids released by `remove` are
recycled by later inserts, so the id counter only grows with the peak
number of simultaneously stored prices and can never be exhausted in
practice (2^31 simultaneous levels).

## Functions

<a id="insert-tree-uint128" />

### insert

```solidity

```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |

| price | `uint128` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| created | `bool` |  |

<a id="_newnode-tree" />

### \_newNode

<i>
  Reuse a released id first; only grow the counter when none is free. A freed id
  is referenced by nothing (its parent, sibling and `leaves` entries were rewired in
  `remove`), so reusing it cannot alias a live node.
</i>

```solidity
function _newNode(Tree storage self) private returns (uint32 id);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| self | `Tree` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| id | `uint32` |  |

### Tree

```solidity
struct Tree {
        uint32 root;
        uint32 nextNodeId;
        /// @dev Ids released by `remove`; `_newNode` pops from here before growing `nextNodeId`.
        uint32[] freeIds;
        mapping(uint32 id => Node) nodes;
        mapping(uint128 price => uint32 id) leaves;
    }
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |

| leaves | `mapping(uint128 price => uint32 id)` |  |

# AsyncOrderLibrary

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/types/AsyncOrder.sol)

**Title:** AsyncOrderLibrary

Helpers attached to AsyncOrder for identity and pricing.

## Functions

<a id="orderid-asyncorder" />

### orderId

Stable identifier for an order, derived from its addressing fields.

<i>
  (chainId, poolId, owner, zeroForOne, salt) uniquely identifies one open order.

  * `block.chainid` keeps ids unique across chains where the same PoolKey can be
    deployed (for example Unichain mainnet and Sepolia).
  * `salt` is contract-assigned at create time and stored off-chain (in the event
    log) so the maker can pass it back when calling cancel / updatePrice / fill.
    `view` (not `pure`) because `block.chainid` reads EVM context.
</i>

```solidity
function orderId(AsyncOrder calldata order) internal view returns (bytes32);
```

**Parameters**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| order | `AsyncOrder` |  |

**Returns**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| \<none> | `bytes32` |  |

# AsyncOrder

[Git Source](https://github.com/asyncswap/contracts/blob/e62a183901a3f5874e378164a989f46ca39dad98/src/types/AsyncOrder.sol)

Represents an async order for a swap in the Uniswap V4 pool.

```solidity
struct AsyncOrder {
    PoolKey key;
    address owner;
    bool zeroForOne;
    uint256 amountIn;
    uint256 amountOutMin;
    uint256 priorityFee;
    uint160 sqrtPrice;
    bytes32 salt;
}
```

**Properties**

| Name | Type | Description |
| ---- | ---- | ----------- |
| key | `PoolKey` | The Uniswap V4 PoolKey identifying the pool the order is placed against. |
| owner | `address` | The maker who supplied `amountIn` of the input currency at order submission. |
| zeroForOne | `bool` | Direction of the order. true => input is currency0, output is currency1. |
| amountIn | `uint256` | Amount of input currency the maker escrowed. Direct matching may partially fill it;<br />unused input is returned when the maker's minimum output is satisfied. |
| amountOutMin | `uint256` | Minimum amount of output currency the maker accepts. The implicit limit price is<br />`amountOutMin / amountIn`. A filler or direct match must satisfy the live minimum<br />for the amount it consumes. |
| priorityFee | `uint256` | Non-refundable USDC bid for equal-price priority. Priority-fee mode requires at<br />least $0.10; filled portions are donated to active LPs, and any remainder is<br />donated when canceled or moved to the protocol FeeVault if no LPs are active. |
| sqrtPrice | `uint160` | Sqrt-price limit passed to `PoolManager.swap` on submission. The hook consumes<br />the whole input in `beforeSwap`, so the pool never trades against it. |
| salt | `bytes32` | Contract-assigned salt that disambiguates orders. The hook computes this at create<br />time from `keccak256(timestamp, block.number, msg.sender, owner, amountIn,<br/>amountOutMin, priorityFee)` and emits it in `AsyncOrderCreated` so the maker can reference the<br />order in cancel / updatePrice. Submitters pass `bytes32(0)` on create — the value<br />in this slot is only read on cancel / updatePrice / fill paths. |
